examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Transmission delay is packet bits divided by bit rate; propagation is distance divided by signal speed. They are physically different and do not replace one another. End-to-end transfer includes processing, queueing and protocol effects when specified. Bottleneck rate limits steady throughput. Bandwidth–delay product measures in-flight bits over the chosen delay, which must be labelled as one-way or RTT. Convert bytes to bits before using bit rates.

**Key relationship:** Ttrans=L/R; Tprop=d/v; bandwidth–delay product=rate×delay

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Normalize units.
2. Separate serialization and propagation.
3. Account for pipeline and bottleneck assumptions.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Transmission delay is packet bits/rate; propagation delay is distance/propagation speed. Throughput of a long flow is limited by the bottleneck link, while latency adds relevant per-hop delays. The bandwidth-delay product counts data in flight; distinguish a one-way product from an RTT-based sender-window requirement.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A 20 Mbps link has one-way propagation delay 5 ms. How many data bits can be in flight on the link?

**Answer: 100000.** Bandwidth-delay product=20·10⁶ bits/s×0.005 s=100000 bits. An RTT-based continuous-send window would cover roughly twice this propagation amount plus any serialization convention.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Convert bytes to bits before dividing by a bit rate. Decimal network prefixes and binary memory prefixes can be different.

Mbps and MB/s differ by a factor of eight before prefix conventions are considered.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

A 1000-byte packet on an 8 Mbps link has serialization time:

- **A.** 8 ms
- **B.** 125 ms
- **C.** 1 s
- **D.** 1 ms

**Answer: D.** 1000 bytes=8000 bits. 8000/(8×10⁶)=0.001 s=1 ms.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Propagation depends on distance and speed
- **B.** Serialization depends on packet length and rate
- **C.** Increasing bandwidth necessarily lowers propagation delay
- **D.** A bottleneck can limit throughput

**Answer: A, B, D.** Propagation is a physical travel time independent of transmission rate under the stated medium.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

A 10 Mbps connection with RTT 40 ms needs how many bytes in flight to fill its bandwidth–RTT product?



**Answer: 50000.** 10×10⁶·0.04=400000 bits. Divide by eight to get 50000 bytes.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2026 CS2 · Q21 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/network-performance?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Delay, throughput and bandwidth–delay product. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. With negligible per-packet overhead and path delays, steady transfer throughput is limited by the slowest link: 500 kbps.
2. The file contains 4×10⁶×8=32×10⁶ bits. Transfer time at 500×10³ bits/s is 64 s.
3. Choose **B** under the problem’s ideal pipelined-flow assumption; adding full-file serialization on all three links would model a different transfer scheme.
